title: API 653 Training in Seattle: Tank Inspector Exam Prep
description: Self-paced API 653 exam prep for Puget Sound tank inspectors: terminals, breakout tanks, Ecology's tank rule and seismic checks, with instructor Q&A.
h1: API 653 Training in Seattle: Aboveground Storage Tank Inspector Exam Prep for Harbor Island, Tacoma and North Sound Tank Farms
html:
API 653 exam prep for Puget Sound tank inspectors

Storage tanks around Seattle sit in a thin band between the hills and the water: on Harbor Island in Elliott Bay, along the Tacoma tideflats, beside the north Sound refineries and at the pipeline stations in between. Most of them hold crude, fuels, asphalt or renewable blends, and Washington's oil-handling rules point most of them to API 653. This page is for terminal and refinery tank inspectors, for the NDT technicians who scan floors and shells, and for welders and engineers who want API 653 certification.

There is no Atlantis classroom in Seattle. The API 653 course is self-paced and online, and an instructor answers questions as you work through API 653, API 650 and the recommended practices behind them. The American Petroleum Institute sets eligibility, administers the API 653 examination at Prometric test centres and issues the certification. The course is exam preparation only, and Atlantis is not an API-approved training provider.

Tank farms from Harbor Island to the Tacoma tideflats

  • Harbor Island, Seattle. An Ecology cleanup record for a petroleum bulk storage and distribution terminal on Harbor Island says it has operated since 1948 under three owners.
  • SeaPort Sound Terminal, Tacoma. Ecology describes it as a petroleum product tank farm storing and moving asphalt, distillate oil, diesel, biodiesel, ethanol and industrial oil, with about 1.5 million barrels of current tankage.
  • The Tacoma refinery. Ecology describes the Tacoma site that Par Pacific owns and runs as U.S. Oil as an oil refinery, tank farm and marine terminal, and EIA lists 9,000 barrels per stream day of asphalt and road oil production there.
  • The north Sound refineries. bp's Cherry Point refinery near Blaine, Phillips 66 at Ferndale, and Marathon and HF Sinclair at Anacortes all hold crude, intermediate and product tankage; Marathon and HF Sinclair both name Canadian and Alaska North Slope crude among their feedstocks.
  • Olympic Pipeline stations. A 2022 report by the Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission's pipeline safety staff lists nine breakout tanks on the bp-operated Olympic system: six at the Bayview products terminal and one each at the Anacortes, Allen and Renton stations.

Not every large tank here is API 653 work. Puget Sound Energy's LNG facility on Port of Tacoma property, commissioned in 2022, keeps its gas in a refrigerated tank that, according to the Port, rests on 88 foundation isolators; refrigerated LNG tanks of that kind are normally built to low-pressure standards such as API 620 and API 625 rather than to API 650, so they fall outside the code you are studying.

Which rule sends an inspector to a Washington tank

The same steel tank can be under one rule, two or none, depending on what it is connected to. The table maps the common cases around the Sound.

TankRuleWhat it says about inspection
Storage tank at a Class 1 facility (refinery or marine terminal)Washington Department of Ecology, WAC 173-180-330Maintenance, repair and inspection to API 653 (2014 edition with Addenda 1 and 2) unless Ecology approves an equivalent strategy; seismic inspection to API 653's seismic provisions and the 2021 International Building Code; overfill controls to NFPA 30
Breakout tank on an interstate liquids pipelinePHMSA, 49 CFR 195.432Atmospheric and low-pressure steel tanks inspected under API 653, without its risk-based interval alternative; tanks built to API 2510 inspected under section 6 of API 510; a yearly inspection under paragraph (a) only for tanks not covered by (b) or (c)
Bulk storage container at a site with an SPCC planEPA, 40 CFR 112.8(c)(6)Test or inspect each aboveground container for integrity on a regular schedule and whenever material repairs are made; EPA's fact sheet names API 653 and STI SP001 as industry standards; records kept for three years
Process and intermediate tanks inside a refineryThe owner's mechanical integrity programmeSet by the owner, commonly built on API 653 for tanks designed to API 650, and often overlapping the rules above

Ecology's rule reaches further than many inspectors expect. Its definition of a storage tank covers every aboveground container connected to a transfer pipeline, and any aboveground container larger than 10,000 gallons (238 barrels) holding bulk oil at a Class 1 facility, though it leaves out process pressure vessels and tanks in the process flow. Like the transfer pipeline section, it cites a fixed edition of API 653, while the examination follows the edition named on the effectivity sheet for your window.

Where rules overlap, one well-planned inspection can serve all of them, provided the report says which standard it follows and the records outlast the shortest retention rule. SPCC asks for three years of test and inspection records, but EPA recommends keeping formal test reports for the life of the container, and API 653 expects the owner to hold a full file of construction records, inspection history and repairs or alterations. A Puget Sound terminal inspector who knows which tanks Ecology, PHMSA and EPA each claim can scope a single out-of-service inspection that satisfies every regulator with an interest in that tank.

Seismic checks Washington adds to the API 653 inspection

Earthquake risk is part of everyday tank work on the Sound, and Ecology's 2023 amendments to WAC 173-180-330 wrote it into the inspection programme.

  • Existing tanks. Tanks built before the amendment took effect need one or more seismic protection measures: flexible connections between tank and piping, foundation-driven pilings, anchoring, or an alternative Ecology approves. Ecology's guidance says compliance with API 650 (2020) seismic design requirements can be used to support an alternative.
  • Seismic inspections. Tanks are inspected against the seismic design requirements of API 653 and the applicable 2021 IBC provisions, and the results feed the facility's spill risk analysis.
  • New tanks. Tanks built after the amendment must meet API 650 (2020) Annex E, ASCE 7-22 and the 2021 IBC, plus tsunami resistance requirements that depend on the facility's risk area.

In the field that means looking hard at anchor bolts and chairs, flexible piping connections at shell nozzles, the shell-to-bottom region and foundation condition. The examination is narrower: the API 653 Body of Knowledge does not ask candidates to calculate shell thickness for earthquake loads, so learn the seismic items for the job and the code's evaluation and repair rules for the paper.

What Puget Sound products do to tanks

  • Asphalt. Heated, insulated asphalt tanks at Tacoma bring corrosion under insulation on the shell, roof corrosion where vapours condense, and heat at the foundation. Inspection depends on stripping insulation at the right places, not on readings taken through it.
  • Ethanol and biodiesel. SeaPort Sound handles both. API RP 571 covers stress corrosion cracking in fuel-grade ethanol, and water that separates from biodiesel and diesel can support microbiologically influenced corrosion on tank bottoms; both mechanisms appear in the API 653 Body of Knowledge through RP 571.
  • Crude. Refinery crude tanks collect sludge and water bottoms, and pitting under deposits drives the floor projections API 653 asks for at every internal inspection.
  • Jet fuel. bp describes Cherry Point as a leading supplier of jet fuel to the Seattle and Portland international airports. Clean-product service puts the emphasis on internal linings, with API RP 652 covering those on tank bottoms, and on keeping water out.

Rain, roofs and the tank bottom

Western Washington's long wet season is hard on the parts of a tank that handle water. External floating roofs depend on their primary drains: a blocked or leaking drain leaves rainwater on the deck, or lets product into the drain line, so drain hoses, articulated joints and check valves deserve attention at every out-of-service inspection. Rim seals and pontoons need checking for water ingress. Around the base, water that collects at the chime and in the edge of the foundation drives external bottom corrosion where the floor plate projects beyond the shell, which is why the annular region gets its own attention in API 653. Underneath, cathodic protection to API RP 651 and the presence or absence of a release prevention barrier change both the corrosion rate you can expect and the minimum bottom thickness the code allows at the next inspection.

Routes into API 653 for Seattle tank people

Annex D of API 653 combines education with tank experience gained in the last 10 years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency: one year with a bachelor's degree in engineering or technology, two with a two-year degree or certificate, three with a high school diploma and five or more with no formal education, the longer routes each including at least a year of inspection. The API 653 certification requirements page gives the full rules, and API reviews every application.

  • Terminal operators at Harbor Island or Tacoma already do the routine in-service checks API 653 expects of owner personnel; the step up is planning and evaluating the formal inspections.
  • NDT technicians who run floor scans, shell thickness surveys and weld examinations on tanks know the data; NDT training in Seattle covers the earlier certifications.
  • Welders and tank builders bring construction and repair experience that counts toward the longer routes; welding inspectors can see AWS CWI exam prep in Seattle.
  • Engineers at terminals and refineries need a year of tank inspection work.

Studying API 653 from Seattle

API 650 is the open-book document that costs Seattle candidates the most time, because so many answers sit in its tables and so few candidates use it every day. Practise finding things in the PDF until the welding, materials and hydrotest sections open without a search. Leave the closed-book topics, such as inspection intervals, corrosion-rate rules, RP 575 practices and the RP 571 mechanisms on your sheet, for short sessions between terminal shifts. The self-paced course lets you work in that order, and the instructor answers the questions a textbook skips, such as which shell thickness a corroded area should be judged against. Prometric lists test centres in and around Seattle; book once API accepts your application, because each window has its own deadline. For more background, see the API 653 tank inspection guide.

Sponsoring tank inspectors from a Puget Sound terminal

Terminal operators preparing for Ecology's seismic and inspection requirements, pipeline companies with breakout tanks and refinery tank groups can enrol several candidates together, some of them preparing for API 570 for the dock and manifold piping. Fees are quoted on request, and each candidate applies to API on their own experience record. Owners who need NDE and data review on Washington tanks rather than training can see API 653 tank inspection support in Washington; in the US, Atlantis performs UT, MT, PT and VT, not radiography.

faq.q: Does Washington require API 653 inspections at oil terminals?
faq.a: At Class 1 facilities, yes. WAC 173-180-330 requires storage tanks there to be maintained, repaired and inspected in accordance with API 653, citing the 2014 edition with Addenda 1 and 2, unless the operator proposes an equivalent strategy that Ecology approves. Class 1 facilities are oil-handling sites on or near navigable waters that move oil in bulk to or from tank vessels or pipelines, so the marine terminals and refineries around the Sound are included.

faq.q: How are breakout tanks on the Olympic Pipeline inspected?
faq.a: Under 49 CFR 195.432(b), the physical integrity of atmospheric and low-pressure steel breakout tanks is inspected under API 653, without the code's risk-based alternative for internal intervals, and tanks built to API 2510 follow section 6 of API 510 under paragraph (c). The yearly inspection in paragraph (a) applies only to tanks those paragraphs do not cover. PHMSA proposed changes in June 2026 that were not final when this page was written.

faq.q: Is the Tacoma LNG tank an API 653 tank?
faq.a: No. API 653 covers in-service aboveground storage tanks of the kind built to API 650 and API 12C. Refrigerated LNG storage tanks are normally designed to low-pressure standards such as API 620 and API 625, and the Port of Tacoma says the Puget Sound Energy tank rests on 88 foundation isolators, a seismic design feature well outside the API 653 Body of Knowledge. Experience on such a tank should be described carefully on an API application.

faq.q: Will the API 653 exam ask me to design a tank for earthquakes?
faq.a: No. The Body of Knowledge excludes shell thickness calculations for wind, earthquake and small internal pressure, so you will not size a shell for seismic loads on the paper. Washington's tank work is different: Ecology requires seismic protection measures and seismic inspections at Class 1 facilities. Learn the code's evaluation, repair and reconstruction rules for the exam, and the seismic checks for the job.

faq.q: Our Tacoma terminal stores asphalt and biodiesel. Which damage mechanisms should I study first?
faq.a: Start with corrosion under insulation, because heated asphalt tanks are insulated and wet insulation is the usual cause of shell loss on them. Then study microbiologically influenced corrosion, which water separating from biodiesel can support on the floor, and the RP 571 treatment of stress corrosion cracking in fuel-grade ethanol if the terminal also handles ethanol. Check which mechanisms the effectivity sheet lists for your window, because RP 571 is examined by named section.

faq.q: Does an SPCC plan require an API-certified tank inspector?
faq.a: 40 CFR 112.8(c)(6) requires each aboveground container to be tested or inspected for integrity on a regular schedule and after material repairs, and EPA's guidance treats industry standards as the way to set that schedule. The SPCC rule does not itself name a certification. When an owner chooses API 653 as the industry standard, API 653's own requirements on who performs the formal inspections apply, and that is where an API 653 inspector comes in.

faq.q: I weld and repair tanks for a Tacoma contractor. Does that count toward API 653?
faq.a: It can count toward the routes that accept construction and repair experience, provided at least one year of the total is spent supervising or performing inspection and the work was for, or under contract to, an authorized inspection agency. Keep a record of the tanks, the repairs and your role on each. API reviews the experience you describe and decides; the course itself does not count as experience.
